implementation_notes: In Node the identity field belongs to the mapper: Sequelize declares it in the model definition as { type: DataTypes.INTEGER, autoIncrement: true, primaryKey: true } and fills it on create() from the driver's insert result, while MongoDB documents get an _id of type ObjectId added automatically by Mongoose (which refuses to save a top-level document without one). A schema can instead opt into an application-generated key with DataTypes.UUID and defaultValue: DataTypes.UUIDV4, or crypto.randomUUID(). The classic key-generator object is replaced by those column options plus the driver; hand-written SQL gets the key from RETURNING id (PostgreSQL) or result.insertId (MySQL) respectively.
pitfalls: A public class field named like the attribute shadows Sequelize's generated getter/setter, so id reads as undefined - declare the type without a field, or use `declare` in TypeScript.
JavaScript numbers are IEEE-754 doubles: a 64-bit key (bigserial/BIGINT) loses precision above 2^53, so map big keys to string/BigInt instead of Number.
MongoDB keys are generated client-side: a reused or hand-written _id value silently overwrites an existing document instead of failing.
